auth_security_basics-1.stem: How should passwords be stored in a database?
options: As salted hashes made with bcrypt or Argon2
As plain text so support staff can read them
As Base64 strings that can be decoded
As values encrypted with one key kept in the code
auth_security_basics-1.explanation: Store a salted hash made with a slow algorithm such as bcrypt or Argon2, never the password itself.

auth_security_basics-2.stem: What is the difference between authentication and authorisation?
options: Authentication proves who you are, authorisation decides what you may do
Authentication decides what you may do, while authorisation proves who you are
Authentication encrypts the data, authorisation compresses it
They mean the same thing in different frameworks
auth_security_basics-2.explanation: Authentication verifies who you are; authorisation decides what you may do.

auth_security_basics-3.stem: Which attack does a parameterised query (prepared statement) protect against?
options: SQL injection
Cross-site request forgery
Clickjacking
Distributed denial of service
auth_security_basics-3.explanation: Parameterised queries keep user input separate from SQL, preventing SQL injection.

auth_security_basics-4.stem: A page prints a user's comment into the HTML without encoding it. Which vulnerability does this create?
options: Cross-site scripting (XSS)
SQL injection
Server-side request forgery
Insecure direct object reference

auth_security_basics-5.stem: Where should a short-lived JWT access token be stored in a browser app to reduce the damage of XSS?
options: In an HttpOnly, Secure cookie that scripts cannot read
In localStorage where most of the scripts can read it
In a global variable named token on the window
In the URL query string of each request
auth_security_basics-5.explanation: Prefer an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie, which scripts cannot read; localStorage is readable by injected scripts.

caching_messaging-1.stem: Why put a cache such as Redis in front of a database?
options: To serve repeated reads faster and reduce database load
To make writes permanent on more than one disk
To encrypt the data stored in the database
To split one table into several smaller tables
caching_messaging-1.explanation: A cache serves frequent reads from memory, lowering latency and database load.

caching_messaging-2.stem: What does a message queue such as RabbitMQ allow?
options: Producers and consumers run independently
Producers and consumers share one database table directly
Consumers read the same data faster from memory
Producers wait until each consumer has finished the work
caching_messaging-2.explanation: It decouples producers and consumers so work can be processed asynchronously.

caching_messaging-3.stem: A cached product price must update soon after the product is edited. Which approach handles this?
options: Invalidate the entry on update or use a short TTL
Cache the price forever and ask the users to refresh
Disable the cache for the whole product table
Copy the price into the browser storage of each user
caching_messaging-3.explanation: Invalidate the cache entry on update or use a short time-to-live.

caching_messaging-4.stem: A queue consumer may receive the same message twice. What property should the handler have?
options: Idempotency, so a repeated message has no extra effect
Immutability, so that the message text cannot be read twice
Atomicity, so the queue deletes the message early
Persistence, so the message is stored forever
caching_messaging-4.explanation: Idempotency: processing the same message again must not cause duplicate effects.

caching_messaging-5.stem: After a cache entry expires, hundreds of requests hit the database at once. What is this problem called?
options: A cache stampede
A deadlock
A memory leak
A race on the primary key
caching_messaging-5.explanation: A cache stampede (thundering herd); mitigated by locking, request coalescing or staggered TTLs.

data_structures_algorithms-1.stem: Which data structure gives average O(1) lookup of a value by its key?
options: Hash map
Linked list
Sorted array
Binary heap
data_structures_algorithms-1.explanation: A hash map (dictionary) offers average constant-time lookups by key.

data_structures_algorithms-2.stem: A stack removes items in which order?
options: Last in, first out
First in, first out
Smallest value first
Random order
data_structures_algorithms-2.explanation: A stack is last in, first out (LIFO).

data_structures_algorithms-3.stem: Binary search on a sorted array of n items takes how many steps in the worst case?
options: About log n steps
About n steps
About n log n steps
About n squared steps
data_structures_algorithms-3.explanation: Each step halves the search space, so O(log n).

data_structures_algorithms-4.stem: You need the shortest path between two nodes in an unweighted graph. Which algorithm fits?
options: Breadth-first search
Depth-first search
Binary search
Merge sort
data_structures_algorithms-4.explanation: Breadth-first search explores level by level and finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

data_structures_algorithms-5.stem: Two nested loops each run over all n items of the input. What is the time complexity?
options: O(n squared)
O(n)
O(n log n)
O(2 to the power n)
data_structures_algorithms-5.explanation: n iterations of n iterations gives O(n squared).

dotnet_csharp-1.stem: Which keyword in C# declares a variable whose type is inferred by the compiler?
options: var
dynamic
object
let
dotnet_csharp-1.explanation: var lets the compiler infer the type from the initializer.

dotnet_csharp-2.stem: What is ASP.NET Core mainly used for?
options: Building web applications and APIs
Designing database diagrams
Editing images and video files for the web
Managing virtual machines in the cloud
dotnet_csharp-2.explanation: ASP.NET Core is a cross-platform framework for web apps and APIs.

dotnet_csharp-3.stem: What does LINQ let you do in C#?
options: Query collections and data sources with a uniform syntax
Link two separate projects into one executable file
Log every event to the console while you are debugging
Lock the thread that is currently writing to a file
dotnet_csharp-3.explanation: LINQ provides a uniform query syntax over collections, databases and other sources.

dotnet_csharp-4.stem: In ASP.NET Core, which mechanism supplies a class with the services it needs, such as a DbContext?
options: Constructor injection via the DI container
A static class that each file which needs it imports
A configuration value written in appsettings.json
A partial class that is generated automatically at build time
dotnet_csharp-4.explanation: The built-in dependency injection container registers services and injects them into constructors.

dotnet_csharp-5.stem: Which Entity Framework feature updates the database schema from changes in your model classes?
options: Migrations
Scaffolding views
Tag helpers
Model binding
dotnet_csharp-5.explanation: Migrations record model changes and apply them to the database.

git_version_control-1.stem: Which command records the staged changes as a new commit?
options: git commit -m "message"
git add .
git push origin main
git fetch --all
git_version_control-1.explanation: git commit saves staged changes to history.

git_version_control-2.stem: What is a branch in Git?
options: A movable pointer to a line of commits for parallel work
A copy of the repository stored on another machine
A snapshot of the working folder that can rarely change again
A tag that marks a released version of the software
git_version_control-2.explanation: A branch is a movable pointer to a line of commits, letting work proceed in parallel.

git_version_control-3.stem: git pull is equivalent to which pair of commands?
options: git fetch then git merge
git add followed by git commit
git clone followed by git checkout
git stash followed by git reset
git_version_control-3.explanation: git pull fetches remote commits and then merges them into the current branch.

git_version_control-4.stem: Git reports a merge conflict in a file. What must you do?
options: Edit the file to resolve the markers, stage it and commit
Delete the file and run git pull one more time
Run git reset --hard on the shared remote repository
Rename the branch so that the conflict disappears by itself
git_version_control-4.explanation: Edit the file to choose the right content, remove the conflict markers, stage it and complete the merge.

git_version_control-5.stem: You already pushed a commit that introduced a bug to a shared branch. Which approach is safest?
options: git revert, which adds a commit that undoes the change
git reset --hard, then a force push to the shared branch
git commit --amend, then a force push of the fixed commit
git checkout of the old commit, then pushing that state
git_version_control-5.explanation: git revert creates a new commit that undoes the change without rewriting shared history.

golang_backend-1.stem: How do you start a function running concurrently in Go?
options: Put the go keyword before the call: go work()
Wrap the call in async: async work()
Call it with thread.start(work)
Mark the function with the @concurrent tag above it
golang_backend-1.explanation: The go keyword starts a goroutine.

golang_backend-2.stem: Which Go package from the standard library is used to build HTTP servers?
options: net/http
os/exec
encoding/csv
text/template
golang_backend-2.explanation: net/http provides the HTTP client and server.

golang_backend-3.stem: How does idiomatic Go usually report an error from a function?
options: It returns an error value that the caller checks
It throws an exception that is caught with try and catch
It sets a global variable named lastError
It calls panic so the program stops at once
golang_backend-3.explanation: Functions return an error value as the last result and callers check it with if err != nil.

golang_backend-4.stem: What is a channel used for in Go?
options: Passing values safely between goroutines
Reading configuration values from files
Opening a connection to a database server
Declaring a type that holds several fields
golang_backend-4.explanation: Channels let goroutines communicate and synchronise by sending and receiving values.

golang_backend-5.stem: Two goroutines update the same counter variable and the result is sometimes wrong. Which fix is correct?
options: Protect the counter with a sync.Mutex or use atomic operations
Increase the number of goroutines to average out the result
Declare the counter as a constant before starting
Add time.Sleep to one of the goroutines
golang_backend-5.explanation: Protect shared state with a mutex or use atomic operations or channels.

java_spring-1.stem: Which Spring annotation marks a class as a REST controller that returns JSON?
options: @RestController
@Entity
@Repository
@Configuration

java_spring-2.stem: What does Maven or Gradle mainly do in a Java project?
options: Manage dependencies and run builds and tests
Render the web pages of the application
Store the data of the application in database tables
Monitor the memory of the running application
java_spring-2.explanation: They manage dependencies and run the build, tests and packaging.

java_spring-3.stem: What does dependency injection in Spring mean?
options: The container supplies the objects a class depends on
A class creates each object it needs with new
Libraries are copied into the project folder by hand each time
Objects are saved to disk and loaded when needed
java_spring-3.explanation: The container creates objects and supplies their dependencies instead of the class creating them itself.

java_spring-4.stem: Which interface lets you get CRUD methods for an entity in Spring Data JPA without writing implementations?
options: JpaRepository
Serializable
Runnable
Comparable
java_spring-4.explanation: Extending JpaRepository (or CrudRepository) gives ready-made CRUD methods.

java_spring-5.stem: Loading a list of orders triggers one extra query for each order's customer (the N+1 problem). What is a typical fix?
options: Fetch the association with a join fetch or entity graph
Increase the size of the database connection pool
Mark each entity as serializable to cache it
Convert the repository methods so that they run asynchronously
java_spring-5.explanation: Fetch the association in the same query with a join fetch or an entity graph.

options: A JavaScript runtime that runs outside the browser
A database that stores JSON documents
A framework for styling web pages
A package that compiles TypeScript to Java
nodejs_backend-1.explanation: Node.js is a JavaScript runtime that runs outside the browser, built on the V8 engine.

nodejs_backend-2.stem: Which file lists a Node.js project's dependencies and scripts?
options: package.json
index.html
node.config
dependencies.xml
nodejs_backend-2.explanation: package.json describes the project and its dependencies.

options: A function in the request pipeline before the handler
A database layer that sits between the app and the storage disk
A tool that restarts the server after each saved code change
A special file that holds all of the app's environment variables
nodejs_backend-3.explanation: Middleware functions run in sequence on the request/response cycle and can modify it or end it.

nodejs_backend-4.stem: Why must Node.js code avoid long synchronous CPU-heavy loops in a request handler?
options: They block the single event loop and delay every other request
They use more network bandwidth than asynchronous code
They are not allowed by the JavaScript language rules
They always make the garbage collector stop running
nodejs_backend-4.explanation: Node runs JavaScript on a single thread, so blocking work stops all other requests.

nodejs_backend-5.stem: In NestJS, which building block groups related controllers and providers into a cohesive unit?
options: Module
Guard
Pipe
Interceptor
nodejs_backend-5.explanation: A module organises controllers and providers.

nosql_databases-1.stem: Which of these is a document database?
options: MongoDB
PostgreSQL
Redis
Neo4j

nosql_databases-2.stem: What is Redis most commonly used for?
options: An in-memory store for caching and sessions
A relational database for accounting records
A search engine for full-text queries
A tool for drawing database diagrams
nosql_databases-2.explanation: Redis is an in-memory key-value store, widely used for caching and sessions.

nosql_databases-3.stem: In MongoDB, when should you embed related data inside one document instead of referencing it?
options: When it is read together with the parent and stays small
When it is shared by thousands of other documents
When it grows without limit as the system is used
When it should be updated separately from the parent document
nosql_databases-3.explanation: Embed data that is read together and has a bounded size; reference data that is large or shared.

nosql_databases-4.stem: A MongoDB query on a large collection filters by email and is slow. What helps most?
options: Create an index on the email field
Increase the batch size of the query
Store the emails in a second collection copy
Run the query twice and keep the faster result
nosql_databases-4.explanation: An index on the email field avoids scanning the whole collection.

nosql_databases-5.stem: Which workload is a poor fit for a typical document database and better served by a relational one?
options: Financial records that need joins and multi-row transactions
Product catalogues with varying attributes per item
Session data that expires after thirty minutes
Event logs written once and read in bulk
nosql_databases-5.explanation: Multi-row transactions with many joins and strict consistency suit relational databases.

php_laravel-1.stem: In Laravel, which file defines the web routes of the application?
options: routes/web.php
config/app.php
app/Models/User.php
resources/views/welcome.blade.php
The ORM that maps tables to model classes
The template engine that renders the views of the app
The tool that sends queued emails
The command line interface of the framework
php_laravel-2.explanation: Eloquent is Laravel's ORM, mapping tables to model classes.

php_laravel-3.stem: Which Artisan command creates and runs the database migrations?
options: php artisan migrate
php artisan serve
php artisan route:list
php artisan tinker
php_laravel-3.explanation: php artisan migrate runs pending migrations.

php_laravel-4.stem: Where should validation rules for a submitted form be placed in a clean Laravel application?
options: In a Form Request class used by the controller
In the Blade view next to each input
In the migration that creates the table in the database
In the route file as inline closures
php_laravel-4.explanation: A Form Request class keeps validation out of the controller.

php_laravel-5.stem: A page loads posts and prints each post's author name, causing many queries. Which Eloquent feature solves this?
options: Eager loading with Post::with('author')
Lazy loading with $post->author in the loop
Caching each author with Cache::remember()
Pagination with Post::paginate(10)
php_laravel-5.explanation: Eager loading with with('author') loads the relation in one extra query.

programming_fundamentals-1.stem: In object-oriented programming, what is a class?
options: A blueprint that defines the data and behaviour of objects
A single object stored in the memory of the program
A function that runs once when the program starts
A file that lists the libraries which a project depends on to run
programming_fundamentals-1.explanation: A class is a blueprint that defines the data and behaviour of the objects created from it.

options: Hiding internal state behind a public interface
Creating a new class from an existing one
Giving one method several different implementations
Running two methods at the same moment
programming_fundamentals-2.explanation: Encapsulation bundles data with the methods that act on it and hides internal details behind a public interface.

programming_fundamentals-3.stem: A Dog class extends Animal and overrides speak(). Calling speak() on an Animal variable that holds a Dog runs Dog's version. What is this called?
options: Polymorphism
Encapsulation
Overloading
Composition
programming_fundamentals-3.explanation: Polymorphism: the method that runs depends on the actual object type at run time.

programming_fundamentals-4.stem: The S in SOLID stands for the Single Responsibility Principle. What does it say?
options: A class should have one reason to change
A class should have just one public method
A class should be created just once in a program
A class should depend on just one other class
programming_fundamentals-4.explanation: A class should have one reason to change, that is, one responsibility.

programming_fundamentals-5.stem: Object creation logic is scattered through the code and changes often. Which design pattern centralises it?
options: Factory
Observer
Decorator
Adapter
programming_fundamentals-5.explanation: A factory (or factory method) encapsulates how objects are created.

python_backend-1.stem: Which of these is a Python web framework for building APIs with automatic documentation and type hints?
options: FastAPI
Pandas
Matplotlib
NumPy
python_backend-1.explanation: FastAPI builds APIs from type hints and generates OpenAPI docs.

python_backend-2.stem: In Django, which file usually maps URLs to view functions?
options: urls.py
models.py
settings.py
admin.py
python_backend-2.explanation: urls.py holds the URL patterns that route requests to views.

python_backend-3.stem: What is the role of an ORM such as the Django ORM or SQLAlchemy?
options: It maps database tables to Python classes and queries
It compiles Python into faster machine code
It encrypts the data before it reaches the database server
It converts HTML templates into JSON responses
python_backend-3.explanation: An ORM maps database tables to Python classes so you query with objects instead of raw SQL strings.

python_backend-4.stem: A FastAPI endpoint receives JSON that must have an integer age. How is this validated?
options: Declare a Pydantic model with age: int as the body type
Write an if statement for each field in each of the endpoints
Convert the request to a string and search it with regex
Rely on the database to reject bad values later
python_backend-4.explanation: Declaring a Pydantic model (or typed parameter) makes FastAPI validate and parse the body automatically.

python_backend-5.stem: A request must send an email but the user should not wait for it. Which Python approach fits?
options: Run it in a background task or Celery worker
Call the email library inside the view and wait
Increase the web server timeout until it finishes
Send the email from the browser with JavaScript
python_backend-5.explanation: Push the work to a background task or a queue worker such as Celery so the response returns immediately.

python_programming-1.stem: What is the type of the value of [1, 2, 3] in Python?
options: list
tuple
set
dict

python_programming-2.stem: Which statement correctly defines a function in Python?
options: def add(a, b):
function add(a, b):
func add(a, b) {
add = def(a, b):
python_programming-2.explanation: def name(params): starts a function definition.

python_programming-3.stem: What is the output of print([x * x for x in range(4)])?
python_programming-3.explanation: range(4) yields 0..3, so the squares are [0, 1, 4, 9].

python_programming-4.stem: Why do projects use a virtual environment (venv)?
options: To isolate each project's packages from other projects
To make the Python interpreter run faster
To compile Python code into a native executable
To share installed packages across the whole computer at once
python_programming-4.explanation: A virtual environment isolates the packages of one project from others and from the system Python.

python_programming-5.stem: def add(item, bucket=[]): bucket.append(item); return bucket. Calling add(1) and then add(2) returns what the second time?
options: An error because the default is a list
python_programming-5.explanation: The default list is created once and shared between calls, so the second call returns [1, 2].

rest_api_design-1.stem: Which HTTP method should a REST API use to retrieve a resource without changing it?
options: GET
POST
PUT
PATCH
rest_api_design-1.explanation: GET is the safe, idempotent method for reading.

rest_api_design-2.stem: Which status code should an API return after successfully creating a resource?
options: 201 Created
200 OK
204 No Content
301 Moved Permanently
rest_api_design-2.explanation: 201 Created signals that a new resource was made.

rest_api_design-3.stem: Which URL follows REST naming conventions for fetching the orders of customer 42?
options: GET /customers/42/orders
POST /getOrdersForCustomer?id=42
GET /getOrdersForCustomer?id=42
GET /getOrders/42
rest_api_design-3.explanation: REST uses plural nouns and nesting for relationships, with the verb carried by the HTTP method.

rest_api_design-4.stem: A client sends a request body that fails validation. Which response fits best?
options: 422 Unprocessable Entity listing invalid fields
500 Internal Server Error with the full stack trace included
200 OK with an empty body and no error message at all
404 Not Found with the client's request text echoed back
rest_api_design-4.explanation: A 4xx code tells the client its request was wrong; 422 (or 400) with error details is appropriate.

rest_api_design-5.stem: A list endpoint returns 100,000 records. Which design is the most appropriate?
options: Paginate the results with a limit and a cursor or page
Return everything and let the client discard the extra data
Compress the response and keep returning most records
Split the data into several endpoints chosen by the client
rest_api_design-5.explanation: Paginate (limit/offset or cursor) so responses stay small and fast.

system_design_architecture-1.stem: What does a load balancer do?
options: Spreads requests across several servers
Stores copies of responses to serve them faster
Sends each request to the newest server first
Queues incoming requests until a server is free
system_design_architecture-1.explanation: It spreads incoming requests over several servers to improve capacity and availability.

options: Spreading the load across more servers
Adding more memory to one machine
Moving the application to a faster language
Reducing the amount of data stored per user
system_design_architecture-2.explanation: Adding more machines or instances rather than making one machine bigger.

system_design_architecture-3.stem: Which is a main drawback of splitting an application into microservices?
options: More operational complexity and network failure modes
A single point of failure for each feature
Impossibility of using more than one language
Slower development of just the very first prototype
system_design_architecture-3.explanation: Distributed systems add network failures, operational overhead and harder data consistency.

system_design_architecture-4.stem: In the CAP theorem, a network partition happens. A system chooses to keep answering with possibly stale data. Which property did it favour?
options: Availability over consistency
Consistency over availability whenever a partition happens
Latency over durability
Throughput over security

system_design_architecture-5.stem: A service calls another service that is down, and retries pile up. Which pattern limits the damage?
options: A circuit breaker with exponential backoff
A longer timeout on each request
More retries that are all sent at the same moment
A bigger database for the caller
system_design_architecture-5.explanation: A circuit breaker stops calls to a failing dependency for a while, with backoff on retries.

unit_testing_tdd-1.stem: What does a unit test check?
options: One small unit of code, tested in isolation
The whole system in a production-like environment
The speed of the system under heavy traffic
The look of the interface on different screens
unit_testing_tdd-1.explanation: A small unit of code in isolation, such as a function.

unit_testing_tdd-2.stem: What is the order of steps in test-driven development?
options: Write a failing test, make it pass, then refactor
Write the code, write the test, then delete the code
Refactor first, then write the test, then the code
Write the code, deploy it, then write the test
unit_testing_tdd-2.explanation: Red (write a failing test), green (make it pass), refactor.

unit_testing_tdd-3.stem: Why replace a payment gateway with a mock in a unit test?
options: It keeps the test fast, repeatable and free of real charges
It proves that the real gateway works correctly
It lets the test run without some assertions
It increases the coverage of the gateway code itself
unit_testing_tdd-3.explanation: A mock keeps the test fast and deterministic and avoids real side effects.

unit_testing_tdd-4.stem: A project reports 95% line coverage. What does this tell you?
options: 95% of lines ran during tests, not that the checks are good
95% of the possible bugs have been found and fixed
The code has no defects in the covered lines
The tests cover 95% of the user requirements
unit_testing_tdd-4.explanation: 95% of lines were executed by tests; it does not prove the assertions are meaningful.

unit_testing_tdd-5.stem: A test passes alone but fails when the whole suite runs. What is the most likely cause?
options: Shared state or order dependence between tests
A syntax error inside the test framework itself
Too few assertions in the failing test
A compiler that ignores the failing test
unit_testing_tdd-5.explanation: Shared state or test order dependence: tests must be independent and set up their own data.
